com.wac.autocore.test

Class OldDatabaseProof

  • java.lang.Object
    • com.wac.autocore.test.OldDatabaseProof

  • public final class OldDatabaseProof
extends java.lang.Object
    L3: a database created before the changes has to start the program and read as before. Section 6: nothing that works today is allowed to stop working. The old database is a file from before the migrations were written, and it is read-only on disk. Every run copies it to a temporary file first, so the proof can be run as often as anyone likes and nothing outside /tmp is touched. The third run copies nothing, because the program has to be able to make a database as well as lift an old one. What is compared is every row of every table, with the money written in kronor on both sides, because the unit is what changed: the old database kept kronor, the new one keeps öre. The same amount has to come out of both.

      • FROM_BETWEEN

        private static final java.lang.String[][] FROM_BETWEEN
        The columns a database from between the two eras has, but the register does not know about. The proof keeps its own list: this is the shape of that era, not a copy of what the code adds. If the code's list loses a column, the first run is the one that fails.

        private static boolean runFromNothing(java.lang.String label)
                               throws java.lang.Exception
        A database that is not there at all. The two fixtures above start from tables that already exist; this one has nothing to lean on, so the baseline alone has to leave a schema the rest of the program can use. A fresh checkout has to start as well, not only one that has run before.

      • isEmptyMarker

        private static boolean isEmptyMarker(java.lang.String table,
                                     java.lang.String column,
                                     java.lang.String value)
        The old app wrote 0 where it meant "no vehicle". There is no row with that id, so the value was never a reference, and the baseline fills it from the booking. It counts as empty, because that is what it was — and it is still reported as a column that got filled.
